name: Antonio DeMarco

tenures.role: wrestler -- a returning MWE original, billed on camera as "The Italian Stallion" and "The Original Gangsta"; came back in December 2008 by ambushing the Intercontinental Champion, wrestled three held matches over the following two months and signed a contract on screen in between
tenures.source: Five served MWE shows, all (the fed's own board, s4.zetaboards.com/MWEntertainment, via the Wayback Machine). promotions/mwe/archive/crowning-glory-ii-2008-08-10.html -- named among the "memorable faces" the arena camera picks out in the Hall of Fame ceremony audience, billed there as MWE alumni. promotions/mwe/archive/adrenaline-rush-2008-12-28.html -- rushed the ring after Sonny Williams retained the Intercontinental Championship and beat him bloody until security pulled him off; later stands on the ramp on Brian Michaels' side of the roster split staged for the main events. promotions/mwe/archive/mnm-2009-01-12.html -- billed by Fred Carry and fought the Grand Mystique to a no-contest, then signed for MWE on camera in Richard Covell's office. promotions/mwe/archive/mnm-2009-01-26.html -- backstage with Alejandro Rodriguez before their match, beaten by him in it, and told by MWE's own board of directors afterwards "we've heard great things about your WcE tenure... but what makes you think you could compete here in MWE?". promotions/mwe/archive/friday-night-overdrive-2009-02-13.html -- fought Sonny Williams to a declared double knockout after two ICW men ran in. Thirteen served MWE roleplays name him besides, one of them his own.
tenures.note: The dates span the earliest and the latest held MWE document that stages him. They understate the character: MWE's own commentary calls the January 2009 match "his return to MWE", its own roleplays call him an "MWE Original" from "the old MWE", and the Crowning Glory II crowd shot bills him among the fed's own alumni -- so an earlier run inside MWE's original 2007-2008 era is asserted by the fed itself, without a single held document of it. MWE's own text also ends the run from the other side: "I am the reason Antonio Demarco left MWE" (promotions/mwe/rp/apparently-i-m-kind-of-a-big-deal.html, June 2009). Neither end is written as a date here, because neither is dated in the record.

tenures.role: wrestler -- a two-time WcE World Heavyweight Champion and a WcE Hall of Famer on his own billing, and the man MWE's own record calls "the only true transition from WcE"
tenures.source: Primary sources on both sides of the wing. From OUTSIDE MWE and contemporaneous: Primetime Central's own Golden Turnbuckle Tournament IV bracket, served at promotions/ptc/archive/gtt4-bracket-himalayas.html (gtt4.primetimecentral.net, via the Wayback Machine), which gives entrants with their home federations and enters "Antonio DeMarco (WCE)" in the Himalayas bracket, losing his Round 1 match to Nick Persia (UWF) -- independently corroborated by Persia's own served UWF roleplay, promotions/uwf/rp/promo-707.html, whose narrator recalls "winning my GTT 4 Round 1 match against Antonio DeMarco." From MWE's own served text: promotions/mwe/rp/your-saviour-has-arrived.html, this character's own roleplay, which counts him "a 2-time World champion, a Hall Of Famer" and puts the replica belts on his own study wall -- "Two WcE World Heavyweight titles, two WcE International Heavyweight titles, two WcE Intercontinental titles" beside an eWa Pure and a WWA HardKore belt; promotions/mwe/archive/mnm-2009-01-26.html, where MWE's own board of directors names his "WcE tenure" to his face; promotions/mwe/rp/highway-to-heaven.html ("DeMarco, is the only true transition from WcE"); and promotions/mwe/rp/going-home.html's WcE roster recital.
tenures.note: The identification of the bracket's entrant with this character rests on an exact full-name match, the bracket's own "(WCE)" home-fed tag, a tournament year inside WcE's own operating span, and MWE's own independent statement that this character came from WcE -- not on the name alone. No second Antonio DeMarco exists anywhere in the held record; the surname does not occur on any other registered entity.

caption: Sonny Williams beat David Whitman and Jekyl in a triple threat at Turmoil for the top belt, took the Intercontinental Championship on the last Genesis, and was named in MWE documents for two years after.
